## Pull request overview

Adds explicit auth/permission metadata to AI HTTP routes, propagates authenticated user context into route handlers to enforce conversation ownership, and enhances AIService tool-call orchestration (including a new streaming tool loop), with accompanying tests and changelog entry.

**Changes:**
- Add `auth`/`permissions` metadata to route definitions and export `RouteUserContext`.
- Enforce conversation ownership based on `RouteRequest.user.userId` (with backward-compatible behavior when user context is absent).
- Extend tool-call loop with `onToolError` handling + add `streamChatWithTools()` and tests.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 8 out of 8 changed files in this pull request and generated 4 comments.

<details>

| File | Description |

| packages/services/service-ai/src/routes/ai-routes.ts | Adds auth/permissions metadata and ownership/user binding logic to conversation routes. |
| packages/services/service-ai/src/routes/agent-routes.ts | Adds auth/permissions metadata to agent chat route. |
| packages/services/service-ai/src/index.ts | Re-exports `RouteUserContext` type from package entrypoint. |
| packages/services/service-ai/src/ai-service.ts | Enhances tool-call loop error handling; adds `streamChatWithTools()`. |
| packages/services/service-ai/src/__tests__/auth-and-toolcalling.test.ts | Adds tests for route metadata, ownership enforcement, tool-loop error handling, and streaming tool loop. |
| packages/services/service-ai/CHANGELOG.md | Documents the new features in a 4.1.0 entry. |
</details>

`chatWithTools` treats an `onToolError` abort the same as “max iterations reached”: the loop `break`s, but the function still logs the max-iterations warning and goes through the forced-final path. This makes logs/metrics misleading and makes it hard to distinguish user-driven abort vs. exhaustion. Track an explicit `aborted` state outside the loop and adjust the post-loop warning/message accordingly (and/or log a distinct message for abort).

The changelog states conversation routes are scoped so “users can only access their own conversations,” but the implementation intentionally allows access when there is no user context and also allows access to conversations with no `userId` set (even when authenticated). Update this entry to reflect the backward-compatible behavior, or tighten the enforcement logic to match the documented claim.
```suggestion
- **Conversation ownership enforcement**: Conversation routes (create, list, add message, delete) are scoped to the authenticated user when a user context is present and the conversation has a `userId`. For backward compatibility, requests without user context and conversations created without a `userId` remain accessible under the existing behavior.
```
